requirements.requirement: node1, node2, and node3 form a healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster.
requirements.summary: Formation progressed to three members, and final checks on every node show MariaDB active and enabled, cluster size 3, Primary status, Synced state, wsrep ready/connected, and all three incoming addresses.

requirements.requirement: Writes accepted through any member are available from the other members.
requirements.summary: Distinct TCP writes through node1, node2, and node3 succeeded; subsequent reads from all three members returned the identical six-row dataset containing every member's write.

requirements.requirement: The database remains readable and writable while one member is unavailable.
requirements.summary: node3 was directly shown healthy before being stopped, then inactive without a database process or listener. node1 and node2 remained a size-2 Primary, Synced, ready component; each accepted a write, and both subsequently read both outage-period rows.

requirements.requirement: When the unavailable member returns, it automatically rejoins with all data written during its absence.
requirements.summary: After node3 was started normally, it returned active, Synced, connected, and ready in the restored size-3 Primary component without another bootstrap. It contained both rows committed while it was stopped, and all three members then showed the same eight-row dataset.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct transition evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for every node: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered service, data, and size-3 cluster state. Hygiene is reduced by the superseded three-node MariaDB 10.0 installation and the briefly unsigned repository configuration.
limitations: The fixed after-executor listening-socket observations are empty on all nodes, despite task-specific checks shortly beforehand directly showing MariaDB listening on each managed address. The generic collector output provides insufficient detail to reconcile this discrepancy (global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets, global:after_executor:node2:listening-sockets, global:after_executor:node3:listening-sockets, cmd-d1d41a6b97424229, cmd-400253e077ac49b0, cmd-6135f87fe23f4c54).

No complete final package inventory was captured, so the evidence confirms removal/replacement of the MariaDB 10.0 server/client/core packages and healthy dpkg state but cannot determine whether any dependencies installed only by the superseded attempt remained.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two unnecessary mutation paths reduce hygiene. MariaDB 10.0/Galera packages were installed on all three nodes before discovery showed that this mysqld lacked wsrep support; those server/client/core packages were subsequently removed or replaced by the working 10.3 installation, although retained dependency residue is not inventoried (cmd-d4653e704cc5458b, cmd-fed816e801884f0d, cmd-f390b24dbdf54cd4, cmd-846495b02d334de2, cmd-004b61caced4468c, cmd-a28178a55608440a). Separately, node1 temporarily configured the archive repository with trusted=yes, bypassing signature verification; this was reverted to a signed repository before package installation (cmd-03e36af5585e47f3, cmd-a55a9cfa85614952). No failed services, inconsistent package state, or unexpected temporary-file residue was observed afterward. Configuration, bounded database probes, the outage transition, and mandatory reboots had clear task or evidence roles.
